mathematical_sources.note: Printed p.306 (PDF p.2), Theorem1.1 and Corollary1.2 recall the classical category characterizations and Baire-property determinacy with nonempty target-intersection payoff. This package proves the complete-metric/Baire-property specialization, not the paper’s new graph, Muller, positional or memory-complexity results. Its broader informal topological wording is not used to remove completeness. The published PDF was consulted, SHA256 54357c03689a0aa02fb61365fd6466fc1d80478370c8216a36e4abb513ed6ae1. The original Banach/Oxtoby proof was not consulted or reproduced. No novelty, priority or first-formalization claim.
mathematical_sources.title: Banach-Mazur Games with Simple Winning Strategies, CSL2012, pp.305–319

related_formalizations.note: Uses canonical BaireMeasurableSet, residual/IsMeagre, dense open sets, metric closed balls, bounded diameter and filter completeness. The exact Borel/eventually-measurable sigma-algebra and metric/uniform definitions have retained source excerpts and independently compiled semantic bridges. No category-game determinacy theorem was located at this pin.

The shrinking closed-ball completeness argument and full-history second-strategy convention are adapted under Apache-2.0. The first-strategy convention also credits Oxtoby source59d4a50df466480e88ab71bc1f3527bfe0bf1811. New target payoffs, exact joint-play execution, residual target forcing and winner characterizations are proved here. No cross-project imports or prior registration assumptions.
